sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

Retrieves and extracts the main content of a web page as markdown.

Include a 'prompt' parameter to have an LLM distill the page down to just the information you need — this saves significant context compared to ingesting raw page content.
Without a prompt, the full extracted markdown is returned (or a structured overview if the page is large).

Batch mode: use 'pages' instead of 'url' to fetch multiple URLs in a single call. Each entry can have its own prompt.
This is much faster than making separate web_fetch calls when you need content from several pages.
The 'url' and 'pages' parameters are mutually exclusive. Maximum 10 pages per batch.

- The gh CLI (via bash) for anything on GitHub — issues, PRs, repo contents, API calls.

Behavior notes:
- URLs must include the scheme (e.g. https://). Plain HTTP is silently upgraded to HTTPS.
- Fetched content is held in a short-lived cache, so asking multiple questions about the same page is cheap.
- Cross-host redirects are surfaced rather than followed — make a second request to the target URL.
- No files or external state are modified by this tool.

AGENTS.md

# Repository Instructions

This file is the entry point for agent instructions in this repository.
Workflows and policies live in the documents under `docs/agents/`; the domain
vocabulary lives in `CONTEXT.md` at the root.

## Testing and Verification

Tests are part of the specification. Write the failing test first at the
spec's pre-agreed seams and make it green with the minimal change — red
before green, one seam, one test, one slice per cycle — per the build
discipline in [docs/agents/issue-tracker.md](docs/agents/issue-tracker.md).
Test-after is reserved for glue and wiring, UI verified by a manual test plan,
and throwaway prototypes. During implementation and review, run the focused
checks recorded under Agent skills for the changed areas and their immediate
contracts; the epic gate recorded there is reserved for the final integrated
epic commit before acceptance and closure.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Gitea issues, driven by the `gitea-issues` helpers.
See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Canonical role names mapped to this tracker's label strings.
See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

single layout: CONTEXT.md and ADRs live per `docs/agents/domain.md`.

### Work queue

Priority lives in the `type/roadmap` issue's ordered queue; see `docs/agents/queue.md`.

### Working standards

Docs and tests are first-class artifacts; the tracker is the queue, repository
documents the durable memory. Read the issue's epic and related issues
before planning; build test-first at the spec's pre-agreed seams; record each
change's documentation disposition and the evidence behind its merge; commands
presented as runnable must be ready to run as written. See
`docs/agents/standards.md`.

### Focused checks

`uv run --locked pytest tests/<area>`

Run on the exact current head during implementation and review follow-ups;
any later change makes this evidence stale.

### Epic gate

`make check`

The complete gate, reserved for final epic acceptance — run once on the exact
integrated commit. On an execution host, run it as
`scripts/execution_host.py gate`, which runs `make check` in a dedicated
checkout at the staged checkout's exact commit and keeps a receipt (see
`docs/runbooks/portable-execution-host.md`, "Run the gate").

# Stage-aware benchmark scheduler

Issue #23 supplies the persistent scheduling and reservation boundary shared by
Stage A and Stage B. It does not launch an agent, authorize a synthetic manifest,
or seal benchmark outcomes; issue #24 owns those operations.

## Frozen inputs

Initialize a ledger only from the exact owner-approved `purpose=freeze` v5
manifest reconciled by issue #165 from issue #50's validated corpus. The
scheduler accepts only the current v5 contract. Recover historical ledgers at
their recorded implementation revisions. The whole canonical manifest digest is the resume identity. The
scheduler rejects changes to the stage, corpus, arm set, schedule, source policy,
resources, outcome contract, or any other frozen field.

A v5 Stage A task/repetition block contains exactly the seven canonical standard
arms, including `claude-code-claude-opus-5`. A v5 Stage B block contains zero
through seven survivors derived from its content-addressed 175-slot Stage A
capability disposition, followed by both RelayView arms and standard Pi, for
three through ten slots. The disposition must bind the exact Stage A freeze and
slot plan; the manifest's deterministic seeded order and outcome slot plan must
also agree exactly before a ledger is created.

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py init path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json
```

Synthetic contract fixtures require the explicit `--allow-fixture` flag and
remain incapable of authorizing a live cohort. Supply that flag on every
fixture mutation (`init`, `next`, `finish`, and `reconcile`); fixture leases are
also returned with `manifest_purpose=fixture` and `simulation=true`. Production
runners must accept only `manifest_purpose=freeze` and `simulation=false`.

Every Stage B operation additionally authenticates the sealed Stage A manifest:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py init path/to/stage-b-freeze.json logs/local/stage-b/scheduler.json \
  --stage-a-freeze path/to/sealed-stage-a-freeze.json \
  --trusted-stage-a-freeze-digest sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa \
  --trusted-stage-a-disposition-digest sha256:bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb \
  --trusted-stage-a-outcome-seal-digest sha256:cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
```

Supply the same four trust arguments to `status`, `next`, `finish`, and
`reconcile`. The scheduler persists the trusted digests and rejects a missing
or different value on resume.

## Owner-managed Stage A capacity

Stage A numerical policy v2 records `provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`.
The owner verifies sufficient provider and Brave capacity outside the runner;
neither the launcher nor scheduler accepts quota observations for that cohort.
The scheduler still serializes each declared account, atomically retains every
whole-workflow reservation and consumption, enforces local and account
parallelism, and preserves typed provider/rate-limit failures. Per-trial token
usage remains provider-reported execution evidence, not scheduler capacity
telemetry.

## Legacy and Stage B quota observations

For a freeze that retains an observation-based capacity policy, provide a JSON
array before each selection with exactly one current observation
for every account that may be used by the next slot. Never include a credential,
token, prompt, response body, or provider payload. A safe observation has this
shape:

```json
[
  {
    "account_id": "openai-frozen-account-id",
    "observed_at": "2026-09-12T13:00:00Z",
    "valid_until": "2026-09-12T13:05:00Z",
    "remaining_workflows": 12,
    "weekly_remaining_workflows": 20,
    "conservative_capacity_workflows": null,
    "recovery_at": "2026-09-12T17:00:00Z",
    "weekly_recovery_at": "2026-09-17T00:00:00Z",
    "external_usage_workflows": 0,
    "evidence_digest": "sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
  }
]
```

`null` remaining values never mean unlimited. An account frozen with `pause`
stays blocked. An account frozen with `conservative_reservation` also needs an
explicit `conservative_capacity_workflows` value. The scheduler subtracts the
observed external usage, frozen external-use percentage, safety workflows,
completed consumption since the observation, and active whole-workflow
reservations. Rolling and weekly recovery times remain distinct in retained
evidence. If only one remaining value is unknown, conservative capacity fills
only that unknown value; it never replaces a known exhausted limit. Every
blocked decision retains the safe quota observations that supported it and the
dispatch or wait event links back to those deferrals by stable decision
identity. Resume replays each decision against the observations, historical
reservations, parallelism, pending attempt, and event order.

Reserve the next eligible slot atomically:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py next path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json
```

For a legacy observation-based policy, append
`path/to/quota-observations.json`. Omitting that file for a legacy policy or
supplying it for an owner-managed Stage A policy fails closed.

The returned lease binds the manifest, stable slot/trial/attempt IDs, arm, task,
repetition, and all account reservations. Pass that identity unchanged to #24's
runner. The scheduler may defer a blocked arm and select a later arm only within
the same seeded task/repetition block. It never begins the next block while the
current one is open.

## Attempt completion

Record exactly one typed outcome and retained evidence digest for the active
lease:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py finish path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json \
  --lease 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 \
  --outcome result_recorded \
  --evidence-digest sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

`result_recorded` binds the complete #24/#131 outcome evidence without asking the
scheduler to reinterpret verifier, termination, delivery, or primary-score
dimensions. Every `infrastructure_failed` outcome requires a nonempty typed
error code. The current v5 policy permits one attempt per slot and no automatic
retry. Incorrect patches, eligible timeouts, unsupported tasks and infrastructure
failures retain their terminal disposition; an ambiguous in-flight attempt requires
explicit evidence reconciliation and cannot be replayed automatically.

Inspect a resumable ledger at any time:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py status path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json
```

## Finite stop and reconciliation

Quota waiting is recorded separately from attempt runtime. After the frozen
cohort end, stop dispatch, ensure no attempt remains in flight, and reconcile
every pending slot as unstarted with retained stop evidence:

```sh
python scripts/stage_scheduler.py reconcile path/to/stage-a-freeze.json logs/local/stage-a/scheduler.json \
  --reason "finite cohort window elapsed" \
  --evidence-digest sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

Do not extend a window, omit an arm, substitute a model, reduce reasoning, invent
a quota reset, or change a frozen resource value to make a blocked cohort finish.
A changed policy requires a new owner-approved freeze and incompatible ledger.

# Continuous Stage A cohort

This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
prepared environment each
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
go/no-go between blocks.

This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
in the order the tools require, up to the
owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
it. The one-task first block keeps its own
[runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).

## What the harness enforces

- **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
  record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
  disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
- **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
  per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
  clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
  appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
  while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
  exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
- **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
  progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
  ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
  completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
  launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
  launcher holds it.
- **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
  An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
  chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
  stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
  rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
- **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
  vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
  that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
  tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
  token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
  launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
  boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
  token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
  service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
  down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
  stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
  past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
- **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
  cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
  a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
  a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
  recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
  native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
  before reservation. Serial
  owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
  makes the checked slot the one reserved.
- **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
  archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
  top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
  ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
  [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
  admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
  Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
  the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
  to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
  of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
  charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
  `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
  (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
  never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
  freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
  as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
- **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
  `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
  ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
  The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
- **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
  `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
  Claude admission and image qualification alike
  ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
  Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
  refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
  home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
  with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
  can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
  and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
  agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
  handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
  `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
  account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
  `agent`, ahead of them.
  An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
  it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
- **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
  environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
  installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
  ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
  Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
  exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
  checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
  Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
  within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable
  ([ADR-0030](../authoritative/adr/0030-require-each-tasks-build-to-succeed-offline-in-time.md)).
  The prepared images live in the owner OCI store with the grader images; the
  execution host's store must hold both (bootstrap's `oci-store` step).

## Portable preparation order

Each step consumes the previous step's output, so run them in this order. Steps
marked **owner** need the owner at the host's terminal (masked vault prompts or
an attestation); an agent never types into those prompts and never writes an
owner record. No step before the launch in step 13 starts a comparative attempt.

0. Refresh the ChatGPT login (**owner**), then re-admit the execution host at
   the final commit. When the cohort moves to another host (attempt 7: asrock
   to Alexander), first move the shared-research ledger and its allocation
   receipt with the [ledger transfer runbook](research-ledger-transfer.md),
   and once the new host is admitted, retire any earlier Stage A ledger it
   still holds ([below](#retire-an-earlier-ledger-on-a-newly-used-host-owner-decision)).
1. The archive allowance ([above](#research-allowance)) and its top-up
   ([above](#research-allowance-top-up-4)) are already applied; they travel
   with the ledger.
2. Export the credential leases to tmpfs (**owner**): the Brave key and every
   provider credential, in one vault unlock.
3. Fresh research and provider admission: the read-only remainder pre-check,
   deployment, Claude enrollment and quota (**owner**), Claude admission, the
   six other arms.
4. Build the plan: configuration, source arm proposal and planning values.
5. Rebind it to the fresh admission.
6. Qualify the release images with the final configuration.
7. Exercise task-input retention.
8. Assemble the unsigned candidate.
9. Owner approval of the exact candidate (**owner**).
10. Publish the approved freeze, once `frozen_at` has passed.
11. Initialize the scheduler ledger.
12. Renew the Claude enrollment for the cohort window (**owner**).
13. [Launch preflight](#pre-launch-checks) once the window opens, then
    [`systemd-run`](#launch).

Merge nothing to `main` from step 0 until the launch. Host admission, Claude
admission (step 3) and the plan build (step 4) fetch `origin/main`, so they
need Gitea to answer, and they refuse with `source branch moved from selected
commit` once `main` has moved past the admitted commit. After a merge in that
window, steps 3 and 4 can no longer run or be rerun at the admitted commit;
recover by re-admitting at the new commit (step 0).
After the launch, merges never block the cohort or a reboot recovery
([below](#keep-the-host-unchanged-while-the-cohort-runs)).

The provider-free [systemd rehearsal](#required-systemd-rehearsal) has no
inputs from these steps; complete it before step 9, since its result is part
of what the owner approves.

Image qualification must follow the rebind: the archive candidate accepts only
a fresh `stage-a-image-qualification/1` whose `configuration_digest` is the
digest of the final, rebound configuration, and rebinding changes that digest.
Fresh research admission must follow the top-up, because new setups take
their account limits from the newest allocation journal and admission requires
them to equal the frozen capacity.

**Timing.** Four clocks bound the preparation:

- The research deployment of step 3 sets a 6-hour deadline
  (`--duration-seconds 21600`): the Claude admission's research probe and the
  six other arms' probes must all complete within 6 hours of preparing it.
- The fresh admissions are valid for 35 days less five minutes from step 3.
  The cohort window that step 8 assembles is `review_hours` (6 hours) of owner
  review, one hour to the start, then the 161-slot budget (2,526,909 s, about
  29.25 days) plus one day: about 30.5 days from assembly. Steps 3 to 8
  therefore have about 4.4 days; step 8 stops if the window would outlast the
  admissions.
- The owner approves within those 6 review hours: an approval recorded after
  `frozen_at` is stale and is refused. Publication then waits until
  `frozen_at` has passed, and the launch until the window has started.
- The Claude enrollment receipt recorded in step 3 is valid for 24 hours and
  must still be valid for the Claude admission right after it. Step 12's
  confirmation then covers the whole approved cohort window (at most 35 days;
  owner decision, 2026-10-06), so the owner does not renew during the cohort.
- The ChatGPT login refreshed in step 0 yields a refresh-disabled access token
  that lasts 10 days. The preparation and the cohort must finish within it:
  the launcher stops before any GPT slot whose token would expire within the
  attempt, with nothing reserved.

### 0. Re-admit the execution host at the final commit

Every launch input binds the admitted profile, and the profile binds its
commit, so the execution host is admitted once more at the commit that contains this
runbook's tools before any provider admission.

First (**owner**, in a terminal on the execution host or through `ssh -t -L
1455:localhost:1455`), refresh the Codex ChatGPT login in the vault and record
it as a same-account rotation of the `codex` enrollment. The two GPT arms
receive a refresh-disabled copy of its access token, which lasts 10 days from
the login, and admission pins the vault's digest, so the vault cannot change
again until the cohort ends. Refreshing first gives the preparation and the
cohort the most of those 10 days. Open the printed login URL in a browser on
the machine you connected from and log in with the evaluation account; the
forwarded port carries the callback:

```sh

  set -euo pipefail
  umask 077
  base="$HOME/.local/share/agent-harness-evals/staged-execution"
  export PATH="$base/runtime/node-v22.19.0-linux-x64/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
  cd "$base/checkout"

  before=$(sha256sum "$vault" | cut -d" " -f1)
```

then the rotation record (`"step": "rotation"`, `"enrollment": "codex"`). The
owner-steps chain then continues from the rotated vault, and its next step is a
new credential-delivery verification for that vault, which §7 requires.
Logging in with another account is a stop: the provider account identities
the cohort admits are the enrolled ones. On the execution host, move the staged
checkout to that commit by rerunning
[bootstrap](portable-execution-host.md#4-run-bootstrap) with the final `main`
commit (`git -C ~/evals/agent-harness-evals rev-parse origin/main` after a

for that commit, in order:

2. The logout survival step that owner-steps prints (**owner**).
3. [§8 Checkpoint and back up](portable-execution-host.md#8-checkpoint-and-back-up),

### 2. Export the credential leases to tmpfs (owner)

The supervised cohort unit has no terminal, so it never unlocks the vault.
Its credentials are two leases on the verified `/dev/shm` tmpfs, never on
disk, so filesystem snapshots and backups never hold a key:

- the Brave key the research sidecar reads (`research_credential` in the
  configuration): `$lease`, the attachment `enroll_target_brave.py` enrolled;
- the provider credential lease beside it
  (`$(dirname "$lease")/stage-a-provider-credentials`): one private file per
  provider attachment the seven arms use (the Claude setup token, the Z.AI and
  Meta keys and the Codex ChatGPT login) and a manifest binding each file's
  SHA-256 to the admitted vault's digest.

The helper exports both from this host's own vault (the registry entry's
vault, pinned to the admitted profile's vault digest) in one masked unlock,
mode `0600` in a `0700` per-user directory. A reboot removes them: re-export
after every reboot, before any step or resumption that uses research or a
provider (the launcher refuses a missing lease and any credential outside the
tmpfs, and a slot's rehearsal stops the cohort before its reservation). Run it
in a terminal on the execution host, not through an SSH command:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -B scripts/export_stage_a_research_lease.py --host-id "$host_id" \
  --host-profile "$profile" --trusted-host-digest "$trusted_host_digest"
```

Expected: one masked `Unlock evaluation vault` prompt, then one JSON line with
`status=exported`, `lease` equal to `$lease`, the admitted
`database_sha256`, `provider_lease` beside it, `provider_attachments=4` and
`provider_requests=0`. No key is printed. `a research lease already exists` or
`a provider credential lease already exists` means they were exported since the
last boot: keep them. The export checks the staged checkout locally (the
admitted commit, clean, with the expected origin URL, at its recorded path) and
never fetches origin, so after the launch it needs no network and a merge to

digest pin mismatch, `not one raw Brave key`, `/dev/shm must be a writable

### 3. Fresh research and provider admission

These steps make live provider requests and charge the conserved accounts:
three Claude qualification workflows, and up to nine whole research workflows
on the shared research ledger, because Claude's access, research and
conformance probes and the six other arms' probes each reserve one. Run no
step twice; a failed probe stops for reconciliation, and its charges stay.

First check, read-only, that the conserved ledger can still afford the round.
Every dispatch and the launch preflight require the live remainder to cover
one whole workflow for each unsettled slot, so the remainder must cover the
cohort's slots plus nine workflows before any probe runs:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -B - "$research_state" "$adoption" <<'PY'
import json, sqlite3, sys
from contextlib import closing
from pathlib import Path
from agent_harness_evals.account_capacity import _active_totals, _state
from agent_harness_evals.research_budget import WORKFLOW, require_remainder
state, adoption = Path(sys.argv[1]), json.loads(Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text())
slots = adoption['summary']['scheduled_slots']
with closing(sqlite3.connect(f'{(state / "research.sqlite").resolve().as_uri()}?mode=ro', uri=True)) as connection:
    quota, reservations = _state(connection)
active = _active_totals(reservations)
remaining = {k: quota['identity'][k] - quota['used'][k] - active[k] for k in WORKFLOW}
print(json.dumps({'used_calls': quota['used']['calls'], 'remaining_calls': remaining['calls'],
                  'cohort_calls': slots * WORKFLOW['calls'],
                  'spare_workflows': min(remaining[k] // WORKFLOW[k] for k in WORKFLOW if WORKFLOW[k]) - slots}))
require_remainder(quota['identity'], quota['used'], slots + 9, active)
print(f'research remainder covers {slots} slots and a fresh admission round')
PY
```

# Continuous Stage A cohort

This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
prepared environment each
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
go/no-go between blocks.

This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
in the order the tools require, up to the
owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
it. The one-task first block keeps its own
[runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).

## What the harness enforces

- **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
  record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
  disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
- **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
  per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
  clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
  appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
  while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
  exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
- **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
  progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
  ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
  completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
  launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
  launcher holds it.
- **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
  An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
  chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
  stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
  rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
- **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
  vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
  that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
  tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
  token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
  launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
  boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
  token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
  service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
  down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
  stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
  past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
- **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
  cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
  a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
  a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
  recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
  native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
  before reservation. Serial
  owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
  makes the checked slot the one reserved.
- **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
  archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
  top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
  ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
  [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
  admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
  Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
  the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
  to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
  of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
  charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
  `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
  (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
  never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
  freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
  as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
- **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
  `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
  ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
  The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
- **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
  `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
  Claude admission and image qualification alike
  ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
  Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
  refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
  home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
  with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
  can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
  and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
  agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
  handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
  `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
  account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
  `agent`, ahead of them.
  An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
  it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
- **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
  environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
  installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
  ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
  Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
  exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
  checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
  Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
  within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable
  ([ADR-0030](../authoritative/adr/0030-require-each-tasks-build-to-succeed-offline-in-time.md)).
  The prepared images live in the owner OCI store with the grader images; the
  execution host's store must hold both (bootstrap's `oci-store` step).

## Paths and shell

Everything except the allowance steps below runs **on the execution host**,
in one zsh (or bash) shell, from the admitted staged checkout `$base/checkout`: the host must
have been re-admitted at the commit that contains this runbook's tools
([portable host, sections 7 to 9](portable-execution-host.md#7-qualify-the-host)),
because every launch input binds the admitted profile's commit. From attempt 7
the execution host is `cachyos-alexander` (`alexander-evals`, battery-backed,
on the dedicated eval daemon); attempts 3 to 6 ran on `cachyos-asrock`,
and the allowance steps were applied there. `host_id` and `vault` come from the
registry entry this machine verifies as. The operator
checkout `~/evals/agent-harness-evals` is used only where a section says so.
The launcher requires the admitted profile's paths: the ledger is
`state/stage-a/scheduler.json` and the artifact root `artifacts/stage-a/live`
under the staged-execution root. Any other ledger or artifact path is refused
(`launcher must use the admitted target-local ledger and artifact paths`).

Start every session with these assignments. They change nothing; rerun them in
a new shell and continue where you stopped. `attempt` names one private
working directory for this cohort's plan, evidence and gate; a refused or
abandoned attempt keeps its directory and the next one uses `attempt=2`. An
attempt whose cohort launched and stopped is first
[retired](#retire-a-stopped-attempt-owner-decision), which moves its ledger and
artifact root into its own directory.

```sh

release=stage-a-prepared-23-v1

export PATH="$base/runtime/node-v22.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
```

complete new `4→3→2→1` chain authenticated before commit. It cannot repeat. A
refusal prints only `Amendment rejected; retain any backup and reconcile the
journal before retrying.` After any refusal or uncertain result, rerun the
read-only block before anything else: it prints `stage-a-research-allocation/4`
and the `receipt_digest` once the top-up is applied (its remainder column then
reads against the same top-up identity), and `stage-a-research-allocation/3`
while it is not. Never rerun a completed top-up or restore its backup over
newer usage. The [Paths and shell](#paths-and-shell) `allocation` names this
receipt; the step-4 builder and candidate assembly take it, and refuse the
superseded `/3` receipt.

## Portable preparation order

Each step consumes the previous step's output, so run them in this order. Steps
marked **owner** need the owner at the host's terminal (masked vault prompts or
an attestation); an agent never types into those prompts and never writes an
owner record. No step before the launch in step 13 starts a comparative attempt.

0. Refresh the ChatGPT login (**owner**), then re-admit the execution host at
   the final commit. When the cohort moves to another host (attempt 7: asrock
   to Alexander), first move the shared-research ledger and its allocation
   receipt with the [ledger transfer runbook](research-ledger-transfer.md),
   and once the new host is admitted, retire any earlier Stage A ledger it
   still holds ([below](#retire-an-earlier-ledger-on-a-newly-used-host-owner-decision)).
1. The archive allowance ([above](#research-allowance)) and its top-up
   ([above](#research-allowance-top-up-4)) are already applied; they travel
   with the ledger.
2. Export the credential leases to tmpfs (**owner**): the Brave key and every
   provider credential, in one vault unlock.
3. Fresh research and provider admission: the read-only remainder pre-check,
   deployment, Claude enrollment and quota (**owner**), Claude admission, the
   six other arms.
4. Build the plan: configuration, source arm proposal and planning values.
5. Rebind it to the fresh admission.
6. Qualify the release images with the final configuration.
7. Exercise task-input retention.
8. Assemble the unsigned candidate.
9. Owner approval of the exact candidate (**owner**).
10. Publish the approved freeze, once `frozen_at` has passed.
11. Initialize the scheduler ledger.
12. Renew the Claude enrollment for the cohort window (**owner**).
13. [Launch preflight](#pre-launch-checks) once the window opens, then
    [`systemd-run`](#launch).

Merge nothing to `main` from step 0 until the launch. Host admission, Claude
admission (step 3) and the plan build (step 4) fetch `origin/main`, so they
need Gitea to answer, and they refuse with `source branch moved from selected
commit` once `main` has moved past the admitted commit. After a merge in that
window, steps 3 and 4 can no longer run or be rerun at the admitted commit;
recover by re-admitting at the new commit (step 0).
After the launch, merges never block the cohort or a reboot recovery
([below](#keep-the-host-unchanged-while-the-cohort-runs)).

The provider-free [systemd rehearsal](#required-systemd-rehearsal) has no
inputs from these steps; complete it before step 9, since its result is part
of what the owner approves.

Image qualification must follow the rebind: the archive candidate accepts only
a fresh `stage-a-image-qualification/1` whose `configuration_digest` is the
digest of the final, rebound configuration, and rebinding changes that digest.
Fresh research admission must follow the top-up, because new setups take
their account limits from the newest allocation journal and admission requires
them to equal the frozen capacity.

**Timing.** Four clocks bound the preparation:

- The research deployment of step 3 sets a 6-hour deadline
  (`--duration-seconds 21600`): the Claude admission's research probe and the
  six other arms' probes must all complete within 6 hours of preparing it.
- The fresh admissions are valid for 35 days less five minutes from step 3.
  The cohort window that step 8 assembles is `review_hours` (6 hours) of owner
  review, one hour to the start, then the 161-slot budget (2,526,909 s, about
  29.25 days) plus one day: about 30.5 days from assembly. Steps 3 to 8
  therefore have about 4.4 days; step 8 stops if the window would outlast the
  admissions.
- The owner approves within those 6 review hours: an approval recorded after
  `frozen_at` is stale and is refused. Publication then waits until
  `frozen_at` has passed, and the launch until the window has started.
- The Claude enrollment receipt recorded in step 3 is valid for 24 hours and
  must still be valid for the Claude admission right after it. Step 12's
  confirmation then covers the whole approved cohort window (at most 35 days;
  owner decision, 2026-10-06), so the owner does not renew during the cohort.
- The ChatGPT login refreshed in step 0 yields a refresh-disabled access token
  that lasts 10 days. The preparation and the cohort must finish within it:
  the launcher stops before any GPT slot whose token would expire within the
  attempt, with nothing reserved.

### 0. Re-admit the execution host at the final commit

Every launch input binds the admitted profile, and the profile binds its
commit, so the execution host is admitted once more at the commit that contains this
runbook's tools before any provider admission.

First (**owner**, in a terminal on the execution host or through `ssh -t -L
1455:localhost:1455`), refresh the Codex ChatGPT login in the vault and record
it as a same-account rotation of the `codex` enrollment. The two GPT arms
receive a refresh-disabled copy of its access token, which lasts 10 days from
the login, and admission pins the vault's digest, so the vault cannot change
again until the cohort ends. Refreshing first gives the preparation and the
cohort the most of those 10 days. Open the printed login URL in a browser on
the machine you connected from and log in with the evaluation account; the
forwarded port carries the callback:

```sh
(
  set -euo pipefail
  umask 077

```

then the rotation record (`"step": "rotation"`, `"enrollment": "codex"`). The
owner-steps chain then continues from the rotated vault, and its next step is a
new credential-delivery verification for that vault, which §7 requires.
Logging in with another account is a stop: the provider account identities
the cohort admits are the enrolled ones. On the execution host, move the staged
checkout to that commit by rerunning
[bootstrap](portable-execution-host.md#4-run-bootstrap) with the final `main`

2. The logout survival step that owner-steps prints (**owner**).
3. [§8 Checkpoint and back up](portable-execution-host.md#8-checkpoint-and-back-up),

4. The reboot that owner-steps prints (**owner**).
5. [§9 Resume and admit](portable-execution-host.md#9-resume-and-admit):

# Seven-arm Stage A numerical reconciliation

The current 25-task numerical assembly selects the v3 corpus and the accepted
v5 seven-arm contract. [ADR-0015](../authoritative/adr/0015-record-stage-a-successor-corpus-allocation.md)
records the approved `c=3`, `cpp=4`, `go=4`, `js=3`, `rust=3`, `java=0`, `ts=4`,
`cs=4` allocation; the [corpus runbook](multilang-stage-a-freeze.md) gives its
exact identity and read-only validation procedure. V3 retains v2's allocation
and task selection while adopting authoritative test restoration; both earlier
corpus files remain historical evidence.

The checked-in [September 16 reconciliation proposal](../evidence/stage-a-reconciliation-165.json)
retains the historical v1 corpus and is unsigned planning evidence. Regenerating
a proposal now reads v3; it does not rewrite that file or transfer an approval.
The [September 20 publication](../evidence/stage-a-approved-publication-50-20260920.json)
records the separately approved v2 numerical freeze. Its host/profile identities
and dates remain historical; they cannot admit changed source or a new run.
Dated handoffs, interrupted qualifications and window proposals below preserve
recovery context and must not be treated as current admission observations.

Issue #24's current owner decision replaces provider-quota entry with
owner-managed capacity. New executable candidates use
`stage-a-numerical-policy/2` with `provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`.
The owner checks provider and Brave headroom manually before launch. The runner
does not ingest usage percentages, reset times, remaining-workflow estimates, or
quota evidence. Account serialization, durable whole-workflow reservations,
provider-reported token usage, typed rate-limit failures, and the immutable
first-block audit remain required. Historical quota evidence and the prior
Claude capacity disposition remain retained evidence; they no longer create an
operator data-entry gate for the new candidate.

The #50 corpus controls are retained historical evidence. Reuse requires matching
implementation identities; they cannot authorize changed verifier source. Verify the retained checkpoint checksums, match each selected
task's complete validation reference, and compare its image and verifier
implementation identities. Retained `duration_ms` values provide observations
for planning; they do not prove enforced execution deadlines or disk limits.
Keep the corpus input distinct from the final execution-resource admission.

For Claude, `roles[].runtime_digest` in an executable freeze is the SHA-256 of
the installed native executable, as recorded by the host and provider observer.
The `claude_code.platform_sha256` baseline field separately pins the npm platform
archive. The two hashes must not be interchanged. Historical synthetic v5
fixtures retain their archive-based identities; they cannot be relabeled as
executable evidence. Correcting the cohort validator is an explicit
post-qualification evidence-consumer change: native model, configuration,
runtime constants, qualification prompts and provider-visible source remain
bound by the reuse projection, and a new committed deployment still requires
its own host qualification and derived admission receipt.

## Successor image evidence after issue #186

## Conserved Claude subscription accounting

`claude-capacity-ledger/1` implements the #167 owner-approved Max 5x assumptions:
3 session percentage points and 1 weekly percentage point per whole attempt,
two workflow units held back, concurrency one, no credits or paid overflow,
and evaluation-only usage. The historical 12%/2% example yields 29/98 workflow
units before the two-unit holdback; it is never a live reading.

Observations contain both exposed windows, their epoch IDs and reset times,
nonsecret evidence digests, and explicit account/restriction fields. Missing or
stale readings, a provider restriction, outside usage, a changed tier, credits,
or an unaccounted newly exposed cap reject dispatch. A reading expires after
300 seconds or at the first reset boundary, whichever occurs first. Missing
Opus-only telemetry remains the specific owner-accepted exception.

Each epoch conserves a baseline and consumed workflow units. Refreshing a low
rounded percentage cannot replenish spent units. A changed epoch needs a
separate confirmation digest after the previous reset boundary. Only that
window is rebaselined. Active leases carry a conservative whole-workflow charge
into a new epoch; the other window keeps its consumption. Finishing, failing,
timing out or restarting a workflow never refunds its charge.

The numerical policy embeds the pre-freeze qualification journal. The scheduler
retains that exact prefix and rejects changed qualification history, missing or
duplicated attempt charges, mismatched quota snapshots and earlier accounting
versions. Numerical v5 freezes use `stage-scheduler-state/2`; historical v4/v5
fixtures without the extension retain their original state format.

Provider and shared-research workflow reservations are created in the same
scheduler transaction. An exhausted research account cannot leave a Claude-only
lease behind. Claude's epoch balances already include charged reservations;
the generic scheduler subtracts the two-unit holdback once. Deferrals stay in
the current seven-slot block, and the fixed cohort end reconciles pending slots
as unstarted. No capability failure or eligible timeout gains a retry.

## Recovering the September 16 qualification interruption

### Verifier-only conformance correction and evidence reuse

for the retained September 16 qualification. Original reports, research captures,
timestamps, expirations, account observations and charges remain immutable. This
does not permit reusing a previous host qualification as the current host seal.

`scripts/reconcile_stage_a_admission.py check` verifies the original admission,
any independent offline correction and conserved Claude journal. A correction is
required only when the original conformance report failed; an already-passing
report is reverified unchanged. It compares the
complete committed source trees, allowing only the enumerated admission/reporting
files and conformance postprocessing functions to differ. Changes to prompts,
workflow construction, adapters, research, dependencies or other executable source
require fresh affected-arm admission. The retained patch is reapplied to the
frozen seed without executing it on the host; its resulting source must match
the independently scored correction. The correction cannot replace access or
research evidence or extend any validity window.

Run `check` before preparing the fresh host profile and retain its

interrupted cohort by moving its ledger and artifact contents to a distinct
authenticated retirement location before initializing new state at the same
canonical paths; never mix old attempts into the successor artifact root.
Historical reuse wrappers remain authenticated by their file references and
are re-evaluated for source equivalence with the current, more precise source
projection. Only the newly emitted outer receipt must carry the current
projection digest and inspect the current checkout's ignored runtime files;
today's bytecode is never substituted into a historical host observation.

changes must pass the source-tree comparison; the current target runtime must
match its newly qualified ignored files and bytecode. Historical ignored bytes
are never reconstructed from the current checkout. Both the
original and current host contracts remain referenced under their real commits.
Research captures retain their own source revisions, which can differ from both
the original Claude conformance revision and the current host revision. After
authenticating the reuse wrapper, candidate assembly and numerical admission
compare each clean capture's provider-facing source projection with the trusted
revision. Changed provider code, dirty captures and unavailable revisions fail

Numerical admission is a consumer of completed image probes; changes there do
not invalidate image evidence, while image-probe source remains bound.

Fresh host qualification may place its credential-delivery receipt at a new

every research capture. Existing research freshness, inventory, runtime, source
policy and cohort-window checks remain mandatory. Prepared host profiles,

Neither `check` nor `finalize` dispatches a provider workflow or comparative slot.

The prior supplemental correction is now consumable through this explicit path;
do not edit its original `final_stage_a_admission: false` field or overwrite the
